clue.text: Grub female's given to stranger

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
stranger means odder, more peculiar

explanation.surface: A woman's food is handed over to someone she doesn't know.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder is food, especially animal feed, and grub is slang for food.

clue.text: Spoken English as vehicle for Conservative authority

indicators.note: a vehicle carries a passenger inside it, so these words hold the next piece within them

parts.note: spoken means oral, said rather than written

explanation.surface: Spoken English becomes the medium through which a Tory authority speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: ORAL plus E makes ORALE, which carries the C for Conservative inside it after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person or source consulted as an infallible expert.

clue.text: One meeting toff has first raised hat, being careful

indicators.note: says the turned piece comes at the front of the others
in a down clue, raised means the word for hat is written upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
I is the Roman numeral one
a toff is a gentleman, a GENT

explanation.surface: Someone meeting an upper-class gent politely lifts their hat first, minding their manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LID into DIL; TOFF is British slang for a posh upper-class man.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent means painstaking and conscientious, taking great care over work.

clue.text: Material that comes with inventiveness and extremes of eloquence?

definitions.text: Material that comes with inventiveness and extremes of eloquence?

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, a material
art here is skill or creative cleverness

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here of eloquence

explanation.surface: A question about what sort of stuff is produced by wit and fluent speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: REP is a corded cloth; the whole clue also describes witty retorts, material made from cleverness and eloquence.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty conversational comeback, the product of ingenuity and verbal skill.

clue.text: One offers words for politician beginning to tremble with hesitation

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the start of the word tremble supplies its first letter

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A politician starts to shake, hesitating before speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the prompter feeds forgotten lines to actors.

clue.text: Soft, like some ground in the story about sower, say

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
arable describes land fit for ploughing

explanation.surface: Soft, ploughable soil features in the biblical tale of the sower.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sower is one of Jesus's best-known teaching stories in the Gospels, where seed falls on different ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a simple moral tale, and the Sower is a classic example.

clue.text: Herb and little woman hiding in grass by seaside

indicators.note: something hiding in another sits within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: marram is a coastal grass that binds sand dunes
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A herb and a small lady are concealed in the dune grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding in' sends the little woman inside the dune grass; she is Jo March from Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is an aromatic culinary plant of the mint family.

clue.text: Shot getting single in the first test

parts.note: a shot, an attempt, is a trial
in cricket a single is one run

explanation.surface: A batter's stroke earns one run early in the opening Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface misleads: 'test' looks like a Test match but is the definition, and a single is one run in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a preliminary rehearsal or experimental try-out.

clue.text: Retreat in alarm, losing head before a fight

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for alarm goes

parts.note: alarm means fright
a bout is a fight, especially in boxing

explanation.surface: Someone backs away in panic before a fight starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-about is a turn to face the opposite way, hence a retreat.

clue.text: Big hitter provides something dramatic, shortly after defence

indicators.note: says the following piece comes after the first

parts.note: a wall is a defence

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an opera is a dramatic work

explanation.surface: A slugger supplies theatrics just after his team's defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A walloper is someone who hits hard, from wallop, a heavy blow.

clue.text: Making a blunder decapitating fish

indicators.note: decapitating removes the head, the first letter of the fish

parts.note: a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: A chef botches the job while cutting the heads off fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring means going wrong, committing a mistake.

clue.text: Stand and block small stream

parts.note: to brook is to stand or tolerate
a let is an obstruction, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A command to stand firm and block a little watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooklet is a diminutive of brook, a little creek.

clue.text: Steel pad could form such a base

indicators.note: says the letters of steel pad could be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A steel pad might serve as a sturdy foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base supporting a statue or column.

clue.text: Wooden or metal implement confronted

parts.note: a poker is a metal rod for stirring a fire
faced means confronted

explanation.surface: A choice between timber and iron tools to face up to.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker-faced means expressionless, and a wooden face shows no feeling.

clue.text: Predatory bird has a part in darkest religion

indicators.note: a part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hawk plays a role in some sinister cult.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon that hunts by hovering.

clue.text: Supporter of Queen appearing after a short time

indicators.note: says the queen's letters come after those for the short time

parts.note: a second is a short time
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal backer turns up after a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A seconder formally backs a motion proposed by someone else.

clue.text: Offering as a prize an enjoyable time with some servicement

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is a body of servicemen (the page prints the word with a stray final t)
a fling is a short spell of fun

explanation.surface: A good time with a few airmen is put up as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'servicement', a typesetting slip for 'servicemen'; the airmen come first in the answer although the clue names them last.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffling is putting an item up as the prize in a lottery.

clue.text: Dried berries — see 'em about to be eaten by horse

indicators.note: something eaten by another goes inside it

parts.note: a pinto is a piebald horse

indicators.note: about turns the short word round

parts.note: the contraction is written with the letters E and M

explanation.surface: Look at those berries being munched by a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the contraction round to give ME; 'see' is a link inviting the solver to look, not a piece of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is allspice, made from dried berries of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Unsettled on a flight

definitions.meaning: airborne, literally up above the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means undecided, and literally describes something aloft.

clue.text: Leaves one's country that's no good for Middle Eastern states

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is taken away

parts.note: to emigrate is to leave your country to live elsewhere

explanation.surface: People who quit their homeland when it is hopeless head for the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Arab Emirates is a federation of Gulf states ruled by emirs.

clue.text: One with vehicle getting in the way could be rude

indicators.note: the pieces get inside the word for the way

parts.note: Ave is short for avenue, a way
a bus is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone whose vehicle blocks the road might turn rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive means insulting and offensive.

clue.text: Least sensible man at crease, one caught in important match

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, who stands at the crease in cricket

indicators.note: the numeral is caught inside the match word

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A batsman is caught out in a big game.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the batting line in cricket; a Test is a top international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Battiest means craziest, from batty, slang for mad.

clue.text: Sort of ship stuck initially on seaweed

indicators.note: the first letter of stuck is wanted

parts.note: laver is an edible seaweed

explanation.surface: A vessel has run aground on kelp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaver was a ship carrying enslaved people.

clue.text: Swishing sound as a couple of fours get smashed

indicators.note: smashed pieces are broken and reassembled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: two fours, the word four written twice

explanation.surface: A whooshing noise as two cricket boundaries are struck hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Frou-frou is the rustle of skirts or silk, a swishing noise.

clue.text: One who has the clubs but can't play

definitions.text: One who has the clubs but can't play

parts.words: One who has the clubs but can't play
parts.note: sounds like a hopeless golfer, but describes the person carrying a golfer's bag who is not playing in the round

explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's bag of clubs without taking a shot.

clue.text: Still out of work

explanation.definitionFit: Inactive means both motionless and idle, not working.

clue.text: Detract from what could be agreed to

indicators.note: says the letters of agreed to could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Belittling what might otherwise have been accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: To derogate from is to lessen or take away from something.

clue.text: Once again organise holiday destination?

definitions.meaning: a place people go on vacation

explanation.definitionFit: Re-sort means arrange again, and a resort is a holiday spot.
